animation.css
@keyframes spin {
  0%   { rotate: 0deg }
  50%  { rotate: 180deg }
  100% { rotate: 360deg }
}
.spin { animation: spin 2s; animation-iteration-count: infinite }
0% · 0 degin between50% · 180 degin between100% · 360 deg

You specify the keyframes; the browser interpolates eligible properties, while other properties may switch discretely.

Keyframes versus transitions

A transition has only two states: From initial to target state, triggered by hover or click; it plays once and stops.

Keyframes can specify many states: Specify points at 0%, 50%, and 100%; set animation-iteration-count separately if it should loop.

Read the code for state points: Percentages inside @keyframes are the specified points; the browser interpolates between them for animatable properties, while other properties may switch discretely.

What people often confuse

Keyframes decide which states exist; easing decides how the middle plays out. The same rotation with different easing curves feels completely different in speed.

Make the loading icon rotate in a loop: use @keyframes for its states and set animation-iteration-count: infinite. Also respect the system's reduced-motion preference; confirm the icon's movement changes when that setting is on.
